name: Debate & Perspectives
description: Sets up a structured debate: the motion's key terms, the strongest arguments on each side, evidence, a debate format, and reflection. Builds argument rather than recall.
audience: Civics, ethics, literature, economics policy, science-and-society topics.

signals.why: your words ask for a debate
students this age can argue a position

slides.guidance: The motion for {topic} as the title, with a subtitle like 'For or against?'.
Students will be able to argue a side of {topic} with evidence and answer the other side.
Define the key term of the motion so both sides argue about the same thing.
The strongest arguments for and against {topic}, side by side.
One piece of evidence either side could use. Only well-established facts; mark anything uncertain [verify].

variants.guidance: A classroom meme about {topic}. Pick one format from MEME FORMATS that matches the idea, write captions a {grade} student finds funny and that make the correct idea easier to remember. Kind to students, never about a person.

slides.guidance: How the debate runs: teams, speaking order, time per speaker, how it is judged.
Questions for after the debate: what changed your mind, which argument was strongest.
What a strong argument needs, using examples from this debate.
